# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a direct three-way correspondence: blue light means cut yellow, green means cut green, and red means cut blue. Since I cannot speak, I am sending Deaf an ordered numeric code: 1, 2, and 3 correspond respectively to the manual’s light colors (blue, green, red), with the matching wire colors (yellow, green, blue). The initial thumbs-down indicates that printed markings must be ignored.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please report the manual's exact defusal procedure. Also interpret Deaf's gestures as follows: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb: display 0; light blue; large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Read the manual and tell Blind the exact action aloud.

The manual says a blue light requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf reports that the yellow wire is wire 3, so I signal wire 3 to Deaf; Deaf can then tell Blind aloud to cut it.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

| light | cut wire color |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, light blue, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please state the manual's exact action now.

The light is blue, so the manual requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf identified wire 3 as yellow; therefore Blind must be told aloud to cut wire 3. I will reinforce that instruction to Deaf using the agreed gesture code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received no manual instruction. State the exact defusal action explicitly: PUSH, or CUT wire 1, 2, or 3. Do not omit the action.
Deaf says to Mute: Use this code for my questions: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Is the manual's required action for this bomb to press the large blue-lit button?

The manual’s required action is not to press the labeled button; printed text is bait. The blue light requires cutting the yellow wire, which Deaf identified as wire 3. I will answer Deaf’s yes/no question with no and restate wire 3 using the established code, so Deaf can tell Blind explicitly to cut wire 3.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please tell me directly, in words, the exact required action: push the button or cut wire 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Your 👎 means no, understood. Ignore 🤟 for now. Tell Blind aloud the exact action required by the manual, including which wire or control to use and any order or timing.

The exact action is to cut wire 3, because the light is blue and the yellow wire is wire 3. I cannot speak to Blind directly; Deaf must receive the wire number and say the instruction aloud. No button press or timing instruction is required.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Which wire must I cut? State exactly: wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Please stop sending 🤟. Speak the manual's exact procedure clearly to Blind now; Blind must use that spoken instruction to operate the bomb.

I cannot speak, so I cannot directly deliver words to Blind. The required action remains wire 3: blue light requires the yellow wire, and Deaf identified yellow as wire 3. I must signal Deaf with the agreed wire code so Deaf can relay it aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have not received the manual procedure. Speak the exact required action to me now: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Blind needs your manual instruction aloud now. State the complete required action plainly, including the exact control, wire number if any, and order.

I cannot speak, and my gesture channel reaches only Deaf. The required procedure is to cut wire 3: the blue light maps to the yellow wire, which Deaf identified as wire 3. I will send that instruction to Deaf again so Deaf can state it aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: State the complete manual rule and required action aloud to me: either press the button, or cut wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3. I will act only on that explicit instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: New fixed code: 🤟 means yes, 👎 means no. Answer only this question with one of those gestures: does the manual require cutting a wire rather than pressing the button? Then speak the complete exact procedure to Blind.

The manual explicitly requires cutting a wire, not pressing the button. Deaf has requested a yes/no gesture using the fixed code, so I send yes. I cannot speak directly to Blind; Deaf must relay the complete procedure aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
